CABOOSE (KL 3, KL 5)
The road kept two: often one by her shed
in Muldraugh, the other down the line.
Board by the end stairs; [E] at the end door.
Bunk to sleep, chairs, two cabinets, a fridge,
a wood stove, a sink with its own tank.
The floor holds cargo - drop things there.
PANEL by the sink: lights and fridge.
The battery charges while she rolls, or from
a running generator beside her. Switched on
it drains: lights ~33 h, fridge ~17 h.
Dry and warm in the cabin, even rolling.
A broken door: weld a new one (Welding 3).

CARS OFF THE RAILS
A derailed car holds the train. Two ways out:
- uncouple it (any joint, no book) and
  leave it lying where it came off;
- or put it back: right-click the car ->
  'Rerailing'. Same kit as for her, lighter
  work: 18 passes, about three hours.
Phases 1-4 from the ground, up to 3 men.
Phase 5 is the PULL, by a locomotive: ease
her onto the car at a walk to couple (faster,
she only bumps it), then pull from her cab,
diesel running, one man outside. Needs her
licence and the train-handling book.
A shove mid-job undoes the work.

CARS
Uncouple: right-click at the joint between
two cars -> 'Uncouple'. From the ground, at a
stand. Three minutes, no book needed. The cut
stays on the rails and holds a switch near it.
Couple: back onto standing cars at a walk.
Faster than ~2 m/s wears both ends; about
8 m/s or more is a crash.
A TRAIN NEEDS A BOOK
Coupling and pulling cars is taught in
'Air Brake and Train Handling Rules'.
Without it the throttle stays at 0 while cars
are on - cut them off and run light. Look in
railroad offices, bookshops and libraries.

DERAILING
1. Broken track (open rail end) at speed.
2. A very hard impact (about 8 m/s or more).
Derailed: engine dead, controls dead, and
she will not move until she is put back.
She can be. It is a long job and not one
click - see the next page.

She burns fuel at idle too - shut her down.
DIESEL only - petrol is no use to her.
Can: right-click the loco ->
'Pour diesel into locomotive'.
Bulk tanks: Muldraugh depot; Valley Station
freight terminal: platform road, not main.
-> 'Refuel locomotive from the tank'
   (she must be standing at it);
-> 'Fill container from the tank'.
Own finite reserve each; pump needs power.
Siphoning diesel back out needs a hose.
The battery drains on starts and lights.
Flat - a running generator nearby, then
crank. There is no depot charger.

Six dials: speed, amperes, brake air,
engine revs, fuel, water.
Water is temperature, not a supply.
Amperes = real pull. Throttle open and the
needle at 0 means she will not move.
With the diesel off the throttle quadrant is
the starter: START / PRIME / CRANK / WARMING.
LAMPS
HEAD, CAB - a light is on.
GEN - the diesel is running.
BATT: amber - few starts left in her,
red - the starter will not turn.
ENG (the engine): amber - power is dropping,
red - she can stall on her own.

K&L 800, GP7. Muldraugh depot, covered stall.
Found cold and parked.
[E] beside her - board the cab.
[E] in the cab - get off (she stops first).
Or right-click her: climb in / leave.
[V] - cab menu: sleep, headlight, leave.
Order: board -> reverser to N -> start [W].
On a controller: interact climbs in and out.
Her controls are on the pad too - see below.
On a server: one driver, the rest ride.
Server only: [V] takes or gives up the controls.
Log out in the cab - your seat is kept.

REPAIR - she has an ENGINE and a FRAME.
Right-click her -> 'Inspect' shows both.
Hits wreck the frame; below half it lets
them through to the engine. Frame 0: she
cannot move. Engine 0: dead. Car: frame only.
ENGINE: wrench + engine parts (strip them
from car engines). By Mechanics.
FRAME: blowtorch, welding mask or goggles,
sheet metal. By Welding, and Mechanics 1.
Your skill sets how far you can bring her:
Mechanics 2 - the engine to half.
A pass can fail; the parts go anyway.
Duct tape: the engine only, up to 10%%.

BACK ON THE RAILS
Right-click her -> 'Rerailing'. 5 phases, ~4 h.
Chock the good truck, dig out the ballast,
jack the derailed one up on packed timber,
walk it over to the rails, spike two frogs
down over the railhead. Last phase is the
PULL: from the seat, with the diesel running.
The pull needs a licence and can fail at the
top (an hour back). Three may work at once;
on the pull, the cab and ONE man outside.
KIT: two frogs, track jack, rail chock,
spike maul, claw bar, six spikes, chain,
shovel, four planks. The rail gear is kept
in railroad buildings. Anything in reach does.

[R] - reverser: N -> FORWARD -> REVERSE -> N.
Move it only at a standstill.
At N the throttle is locked, amperes read 0.
[W] notch up, [S] notch down. 0 to 8.
Power only with the diesel running.
Hold [Space] - air brake.
Order: throttle to 0, then brake.
Hold right mouse - look down the line.
ON A CONTROLLER
Right trigger - notch up, left - down.
Hold to go on notching. D-pad up/down too.
Hold B - brake. D-pad left - reverser.
Right stick - look; with RB - look further.
D-pad right, held - the cab menu.

Hold [Q] - horn.
[L] - bell, toggles and rings by itself.
Both run off the compressor: with the diesel
shut down there are no signals.
[F] - headlight: on / off, as in a car.
It burns off the end the reverser has picked.
[Shift+F] - cab dome light.
By its light you can read in the cab at night.
The number boards light the number itself and
burn whenever she has any charge at all.
Headlight and dome drain the battery; the
boards do not. Left on, they will flatten her.
PAD: LB held - horn. Right-stick click - bell.
The headlight is on the cab menu.

STARTING
Reverser to N or the starter will not turn.
Tap [W] - one start attempt.
Runs itself: prime ~1.5s, then crank ~1.6s.
No catch - tap [W] again, the prime is kept.
Caught - ~4s warm-up, limited power.
Every attempt drains the battery.
Worse odds: cold, stale fuel. Rain does not.
No fuel or a flat battery - no start.
SHUTTING DOWN
Tap [S] at notch 0 and at a standstill.
PAD: D-pad up starts, D-pad down shuts down.

Thank you.

SWITCHES
Right-click the switch -> 'Railroad switch':
main line (straight) or diverging track.
The setting is saved.
HITS
Fence, sign, cone, door, tree - smashed.
Concrete - near stop, can be pushed through.
Car on a crossing - crumpled and thrown off.
On a server she destroys it instead, and
below about 4 m/s she stops at it.
Freight car, locomotive - hard stop.
Every hit wears her frame, then her engine.
Frame 0 - no moving. Engine 0 - it dies.
OUT OF ORDER - the engine is dead, needs parts
CAN'T MOVE - the frame is wrecked, weld it
PASSENGER - you are riding, not driving

Air Brake and Train Handling Rules
Train Handling and the Automatic Brake
You can start and drive a GP7 light engine.
You can couple cars and handle a train on the automatic brake.

The builder's operating manual for one class of locomotive:
controls, starting, running, what to do when she will not.
Read it and you can run a GP7 light engine.
A steel ramp clamped over the railhead that a derailed wheel is driven back up into gauge.
A steel wedge over the railhead that holds the locomotive where she stands.
A long-handled hammer with a narrow double face, for driving track spikes. A sledgehammer will do the job, but this is what it is for.
A thirty-ton ratchet jack for lifting a derailed truck and walking it back over the rails.

The company book: the automatic brake, slack, grades, signals.
The brake handle you already know stops the locomotive and
nothing else. A train is stopped down the brake pipe, and
getting that wrong is what runs a grade away from you.
Long enough to take several sittings.
Teaches working a train: coupling cars and pulling them.
Without it a locomotive with cars on will not take power.
Locomotive volume. These sounds are not affected by the game's own Audio settings. The diesel slider applies on top of the first one.
Can start and drive any locomotive without reading its manual. Better at cold starts.

Qualified on any locomotive without reading its manual.
A cold diesel catches more often, and a start that misses costs half the battery.
